articles.title: CJP plans to take ‘Cockroach Club’ across India, shifts youth movement beyond street protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Moving beyond street mobilisation, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is looking to build a nationwide network of cultural and discussion spaces with its newly launched ‘Cockroach Club’. The party wants the initiative to reach every part of the country, including remote villages, as it seeks to give young people a platform to debate public issues, exchange ideas and envision the future they want for India, its co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka said during an interaction with The Hindu.

The club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21 and brought together more than 300 people for an event lasting around three hours. The programme featured comedy, satire and conversations on Mahatma Gandhi, while participants discussed local issues concerning Maharashtra. Performances addressing larger issues facing the country were also part of the event.

“This is a platform where we can all come together and articulate the future we want for ourselves and answer some difficult questions we want to address. The idea of Cockroach Clubs is to have a space where people can come, talk, brainstorm, collaborate and envision what they want our country to be,” Mr. Ranka said.

Explaining why Pune was chosen for the first gathering, he said the party had a large support base in Maharashtra, while Delhi was also an important centre for the organisation and would soon feature in its plans.
“The idea is for the Cockroach Club to go to every corner of the country. This is a truly national movement and everything has to come together,” he added.

CJP co-convenor Saurav Das said the club was envisioned as a “physical space for the younger generation” to come together, exchange ideas, question, learn and grow. It would host lectures and discussions on the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, B.R. Ambedkar and other thinkers, besides film screenings, live performances and stand-up comedy.
The space would also offer young people a quiet corner to read, study, and prepare for examinations, while allowing them to unwind and interact, he said.

“This was just a trailer. As we go ahead, we will know what can be bettered. We will use this platform to discuss how to take this movement forward, how to get more and more people to join, and channelise the energy of the youth in a structured manner to bring a change in the country,” Mr. Das said.

He said the club would encourage young people to think for themselves rather than have opinions handed down to them or ideologies imposed on them. “We the young will develop our Idea of India at the Cockroach Club,” he said.
Over 300 people gathered at the Gandhi Bhavan, Kothrud in Pune for Cockroach Club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

The first event was not ticketed, Mr. Ranka said. The local Pune team initially pooled money to organise the event, followed by local fundraising. A collection was also made at the venue, where participants contributed to their capacity.
The party is yet to decide how it will fund the initiative as it expands. It could consider introducing tickets for future events or continue with the local fundraising model, he said.

articles.title: NHAI yet to act despite 300 complaints of inordinate delay at Chowlagere toll plaza on NH 75 Hassan-Sakleshpur section
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Road users have alleged frequent delays in clearing of the vehicles, particularly those with annual FASTag at the Chowlagere Toll Plaza on Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and Sakleshpur and rude behaviour by the personnel manning the facility.

Chowlagere toll plaza near Alur in Hassan district is a part of NH 75 four-lane project between Hassan and Maranahalli (about 45 km) executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The four-lane work got completed a couple of years ago with much delay.

Annoyed with the frequent delays faced by him personally, P. Aditya Narayan from Puttur, a regular traveller on the section sought details of similar complaints under the Right to Information Act from the NHAI. For his surprise, a November 20 reply from the Authority informed that as many as 300 complaints were made to the NHAI, 205 through the Rajmarg Yatra Portal and 95 through 1033 NHAI Helpline between April and November 15, 2026.

During the period, three complaints were received about the staff misbehaviour with road users, the Authority said in the reply. Majority of the causes for the delay in lifting of the toll barrier included software problem, connection failure and a few issues of hardware failure, the reply said.

Mr. Narayan said the scanner often took an unusually long time to read the FASTag. “We were forced to wait, honk twice or thrice and eventually the toll staff contact the control room over walkie-talkie, communicate the vehicle number and get the passage cleared manually.”

After he brought the issue to MLC Kishore Kumar’s notice, the legislator wrote to the NHAI to immediately address the issue. Still, the Authority has not rectified the mistake in the system, he regretted.

Janekere Paramesh, a photojournalist from Sakleshpur who often travels to Hassan, endorses the complaints and said ever since the Chowlagere toll plaza was commissioned, road users have been facing problems of delayed clearance. Rude behaviour by the plaza personnel adds to the agony of road users, he said adding en-number of complaints to the Authority have remained unaddressed.
Mr. Narayan further said FASTag annual pass-holders face similar delays in many other toll plazas across the State.

Stating that the NHAI does not directly handle FASTag issues, as it is being dealt with by Indian Highways Management Company Ltd., the Authority’s Karnataka Regional Officer V. P. Brahmankar told The Hindu that he would raise the issue with its CEO regarding the System Integrator or changing the Integrator. “I will ask the CEO to verify the system and take necessary steps to update it,” he said.

NHAI Hassan Project Implementation Unit (PIU) Director K. Mathivanan told The Hindu that the Chowlagere Plaza was among the many where the Authority used a new construction design to save on space and buildings. There were some ‘frequency’ issues [between the FASTag and the reader] because of the narrow toll lanes. “We will resolve the issue by immediately taking it up with the IHMCL,” he said.

articles.title: JKSSB exam cheating racket: Six more arrested; six government employees among accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six more persons were arrested in the ongoing investigation into the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted recently by Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board, taking the total arrests to 20, with police clarifying that the malpractice was confined to a specific examination centre and did not involve a paper leak.

The accused include six government employees, among them the alleged mastermind. Police said the question paper was allegedly taken out of the examination centre, photographed and circulated among selected candidates through Telegram.
14 arrested as J&K Police bust exam cheating racket; mobiles, wireless sets seized

The investigation has also revealed financial transactions of ₹1.80 lakh, of which ₹1.40 lakh has been recovered, while the accused had allegedly negotiated payments of ₹10–12 lakh from candidates in exchange for helping them clear the examination, Jammu Senior Superintendent of Police Joginder Singh said at a press conference in Jammu.

On November 15, police in Jammu arrested 14 suspects ahead of the FAA exam, “uncovering” a network that planned to transmit answers to select candidates inside the exam centres through electronic communication devices.
Several wireless radio sets were seized in the intelligence-based operation, three FIRs were lodged, and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the alleged conspiracy.

Disclosing details of the investigation, the SSP said the probe had led to the identification and arrest of the alleged main kingpin, whose interrogation brought to light a wider network involving candidates, government employees and other intermediaries.

"Of the 20 persons arrested so far, six are government employees. Their details have been shared with the respective departments for departmental action. At the same time, criminal proceedings are also being pursued based on their alleged roles," he said, clarifying that none of the arrested persons belonged to the JKSSB.
According to the investigation, Mr. Singh said the alleged mastermind had initially planned to facilitate cheating for two persons — a close relative and a friend.

However, another accused involved in the operation allegedly created a separate network and contacted 20 to 22 additional candidates. He reportedly collected their original documents and obtained blank cheques from four to five candidates, with an understanding that payments would be made after they successfully cleared the examination.

Police said the question paper was accessed with the alleged assistance of an employee posted at the examination centre. After the examination began, papers placed on the desks of absent candidates were collected and taken to a designated room. “The employee allegedly removed one of the papers and handed it to another person, as he could not leave the examination centre,” the SSP said.

He said the second person then passed it on to an accused waiting outside, who allegedly took it to his car, photographed it and returned it for deposit at the centre. The photographs were subsequently circulated through a Telegram group to facilitate cheating by selected candidates.

articles.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue ‘leaves options open’ for Pakistan SCO meets next year, say sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The visit of Pakistan Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Musadik Malik, to India, the first by any senior Pakistani official since 2023, was a “Shanghai Cooperation Organisation” (SCO) initiative, not an Indian one alone, said officials as the government came under criticism from the Opposition.

However, former Indian diplomats who served in Pakistan said the visit and the invitation to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi and the SCO Summit to be held in Pakistan next year could be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility” and providing a multilateral platform for the region, when bilateral moves, and the SAARC Summit are not taking place.

Ministry of External Affairs officials have stressed that there were no “bilateral” or one-to-one meetings during the three-day event hosted at Delhi’s iconic Purana Kila (Old Fort) monument. Ministers from six countries – Pakistan, Tajikistan, Nepal, Azerbaijan, Iran, and the Kyrgyz Republic – and Deputy Ministers from eight other countries participated in the forum.

Government officials pointed out that the event allows India a chance to highlight its cultural prowess and strong roots and furthers India’s common links with other members of the SCO, which also see themselves as “civilizational” states. It is also significant that India has carved out a space for itself in the year when Pakistan is the Chair of the SCO, they said, and is leading a shift in the grouping’s more security-oriented and land-locked focus to a more South Asian, oceanic and people-to-people linked focus.

They suggested that such meetings could also pave the way for next year, when External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will all be invited to Pakistan for SCO meetings chaired by Pakistan, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be invited to the Heads of Council meeting to be held in the third quarter of 2027. Government officials said it was too early to speak about participation in these meetings in Pakistan yet, but that a decision closer to the dates would only be possible if options were kept open at present, and SCO events in the run-up to the Summit are kept away from the “negativity” of bilateral relations.

“The meeting was in an SCO context so it would be inappropriate to read into it any bilateral content, leave alone a breakthrough,” said former Indian High Commissioner to Islamabad TCA Raghavan (2013-2015). He added, however, that “given the precarious and fraught state of India- Pakistan relations, an episode of common civility and normalcy is a plus and, even without intending to, creates possibilities.”

Former High Commissioner to Islamabad Ajay Bisaria (2017-2019), who was the last to serve in Pakistan before both sides downgraded ties in 2019, said that Mr. Malik’s visit to India represented “more than a formality but less than a thaw” and demonstrated how such multilateral events allow India and Pakistan to “tolerate each other’s presence, even when they won’t engage directly”. When asked about India’s attendance at SCO events in Pakistan next year, Mr. Bisaria said that the “ball is in Pakistan’s court” to “dial down both terrorism and rhetoric” if it hopes for Indian leaders to travel there. Significantly, he said such an event could be an opportunity to revive the SAARC process as well, that has been suspended for a decade.

On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making the point that while “empires had redrawn maps”, such dialogues had “transformed and enriched global thought”. Mr. Modi had proposed the Dialogue at the SCO Summit in Tianjin in 2025, and the proposal was adopted at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in October 2026, with the declaration announcing that it would be held in Delhi this month.

The criticism was particularly sharp over images this weekend of Mr. Modi and the Pakistani Minister seated in the first row, as well as of Culture Minister and host Gajendra Singh Shekhawat holding a conversation with Mr. Malik at a lunch table.

Several Opposition leaders, including former Ministers Salman Khurshid and Manish Tewari, had accused the government of “inconsistency” in its policy towards Pakistan, particularly the Modi government’s comments that “talks and terrorism” would not go together.

“This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, underlining at briefings held in the past week that the government has not changed its position on other outstanding bilateral issues with Pakistan including over the Pahalgam terror attack, and the suspension of the Indus Water Treaty.

India and Pakistan have at present no bilateral dialogue between them, and since 2016, when the Modi government decided to boycott SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation), they have dropped the regional engagement as well. However, New Delhi continues to make an exception for the SCO, founded in 1999 by Russia, China, and Central Asian states as a security forum to which India and Pakistan were inducted in 2017, and Iran and Belarus subsequently. In 2024, Mr. Jaishankar had travelled to Islamabad to represent India at the SCO Heads of Government Summit.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan entail for retirees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Story So Far: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in a meeting held in New Delhi on November 19, 2026 approved the Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings. As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal.

As of now, a retiring PF subscriber generally withdraws the entire provident fund accumulation as a lump sum. The proposal, cleared by the CBT, say an eligible member, upon retirement, may opt to receive their provident fund accumulations as monthly withdrawals; quarterly withdrawals; half-yearly withdrawals; or annual withdrawals. The remaining corpus will be invested within the EPF Fund and will continue to earn EPF interest on the running balance. The SWP scheme also proposes to provide flexible options to the member for enhancing his or her corpus in PF by voluntary contributions through payroll, direct additional contributions other than payroll and third-party micro-contributions.

articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.

A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.
The cement sector also grew at a series-high of 15.4% in October 2026, compared to 10.1% in September, and 5.2% in October last year.
The fuel-related sectors in the Index other than coal continued to perform relatively poorly.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

• A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16

fullParagraphs: India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year.

European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year.

The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules.

Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive.

The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU.

According to court affidavits, he sent two intimate images from a customer's phone to his own device via AirDrop and accessed the customer's Snapchat account.

Travis County jail records show he was initially booked on June 7 on charges of invasive visual recording and computer security breach under a combined $10,000 bond and placed under no-contact orders before later being convicted of attempted invasive visual recording.

articles.title: Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

fullParagraphs: The 60th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu looks at key developments in public including healthcare financing, reproductive health, antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, environmental exposures and diabetes care.

Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the latest National Health Accounts estimates for 2023–24, which show a substantial increase in government health expenditure and a decline in the share of household out-of-pocket spending nationally. The episode also examines the contrasting trends in Keralam, where household healthcare expenditure has increased and the share of government spending has declined.

The episode looks at the drug regulator’s direction to pharmaceutical companies to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs and the potential implications for treatment costs. It also examines concerns over an illegal human egg collection racket in Telangana, including questions about informed consent, women’s safety and the regulation of assisted reproductive technology centres. Developments in Karnataka’s proposed mid-life women’s health programme and mandatory gynaecological check-ups for girls are also discussed.

Marking World AMR Awareness Week, the episode explores the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and the need for appropriate antibiotic use, timely diagnosis, infection prevention and surveillance. It also discusses phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to target bacterial infections, and its potential role in addressing infections that do not respond to conventional antibiotics.

The discussion also examines tuberculosis through the lens of social and economic vulnerability, highlighting the importance of nutrition, housing and social support alongside diagnosis and treatment. It looks at the latest figures on domestic funding for India’s TB response, which now accounts for 86% of total spending, even as external funding declines.

The discussion also examines the health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women and newborns. A survey of healthcare professionals across five countries found that 98% of Indian clinicians surveyed had treated pregnant women and newborns whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat.

The episode also looks into how fear of diagnosis may discourage people from screening and discusses a Chennai initiative that uses dietary counselling by staff nurses to improve blood sugar control and support long-term diabetes management.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures.

That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says.

Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area.

Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals.

From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026).

A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: Indian team reaches Dhaka ahead of Ganga Water Treaty’s expiry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ahead of the December 12 expiry of the India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty, a team of Indian officials has reached Dhaka for a meeting of the Joint Committee under the Joint River Commission (JRC), which looks after bilateral river-related issues.
The delegation is being led by the head of the Indian side at the JRC, Sharad Chandra. Diplomatic sources said the meeting would take place on November 22-23, 2026.

Ahead of the team’s arrival, India’s High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi met Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman. It was their second meeting in three days, as he had met Mr. Rahman on Thursday (November 19, 2026) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Ganga Water Treaty was signed on December 12, 1996, and was meant to serve for 30 years.
The treaty is expected to lapse on December 12, 2026, unless the two sides agree to renew it. Sources have not clearly indicated whether it would be renewed for another three decades.
India has described the JRC as a “structured mechanism” for discussions on river-related matters, but it is not clear whether the JRC has the mandate to renew the treaty.
The five-member Indian delegation is led by Mr. Chandra, Commissioner (FM), Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation.

Other members are Sanjay Kumar Gangwar, Chief Engineer, Central Water Commission; Ramesh Raj Sambharia, Senior Joint Commissioner-I (FM); and Kanneluru Gautam, Under Secretary, Integrated Finance Division of the Department. The team is expected to be assisted by officials from the Indian High Commission in Dhaka.

articles.title: ASHAs reject government’s assurance; decide to continue protest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The second round of talks between the State government and protesting ASHAs ended inconclusively on Saturday, with the workers rejecting the government’s assurance on a pay hike and deciding to continue their agitation, which entered its fifth day.

Health Minister U.T. Khader had invited representatives of the Karnataka State Samyukta ASHA Workers’ Union for discussions. The delegation included union president K. Somashekar, secretary D. Nagalakshmi and other office-bearers.

The talks failed after the Minister said the demand for an increase in remuneration would be discussed during the preparation of the next State Budget. The workers refused to accept the assurance and decided to continue their protest.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to the protesting ASHAs to withdraw their agitation, expressing sympathy for their hardships and acknowledging their contribution to the healthcare system.
Mr. Shivakumar said the government was considering a comprehensive and lasting solution to their demands and would discuss the matter with the Cabinet before taking an appropriate decision.

“Please respond to my appeal and withdraw your agitation. We respect your service, hard work and sacrifice. The government is committed to addressing your demands and finding an appropriate solution,” he said, appealing to the workers.

articles.title: Skywalk, flyover planned at Konanakunte Cross
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government is planning both a skywalk and a flyover at the busy Konanakunte Cross, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said. “Pedestrian movement has increased with the metro station and the traffic has also shot up,” he said, directing officials to plan a skywalk at the junction to ensure safe and convenient connectivity for pedestrians. He also asked them to ensure that it did not affect or obstruct the proposed flyover construction.

Earlier this year, the special purpose vehicle, Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE), obtained government approval to construct a flyover at the junction, citing increasing traffic volumes that had led to congestion even on connecting roads.
Mr. Gowda said the tendering process for the project is currently underway. He made the announcement after inaugurating the third phase of the Ward One Campaign at Konanakunte Cross on Saturday.

“B-SMILE has prepared a plan to construct a split-type flyover, with elevated stretches of approximately 600 metres on either side of the junction. The project, including flyover construction and land acquisition, is estimated to cost around ₹77 crore,” Mr. Gowda said, adding that officials had been directed to expedite the process and commence work at the earliest.
According to documents available with The Hindu , the SPV had estimated the cost of the entire project at nearly ₹291 crore.
“Once completed, the flyover will facilitate signal-free movement through this stretch, significantly easing the traffic congestion currently faced by motorists,” Mr. Gowda said.

The Minister said the civic body is upgrading footpaths, providing clearly marked zebra crossings, and undertaking road and side marking works to ensure better traffic discipline and safer pedestrian movement. “To further ease vehicular movement, officials have been instructed to secure a portion of Metro-owned land near Forum Mall to create a free-left turn,” he said.

The Ward One Campaign, aimed at identifying and resolving civic infrastructure issues at the ward level, has covered 83 wards in the first two phases. The civic bodies will cover another 41 wards in the third phase.

Under the campaign, specific wards are identified within each municipal corporation, and issues relating to roads, footpaths, street lighting, tree branch clearance, potholes and garbage management are addressed through coordinated interventions.

“Although the campaign was initially scheduled to be completed by November, it will now continue into December to ensure that sanitation and other improvement works are carried out effectively at the grassroots level,” he said.

fullParagraphs: A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu .
The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces.

“Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said.
During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money.

“He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined.

After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database.

The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach.

The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised.

While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said.
As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action.

articles.title: TGSPDCL sub-engineer caught taking ₹30,000 bribe in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A sub-engineer of the Telangana Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TGSPDCL) was caught red-handed by the Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) while allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹30,000 at the complainant’s residence in Hyderabad on Saturday, November 21.

The accused, G. Santosh Anand, sub-engineer at the Gandhi Nagar Section Office of TGSPDCL, had initially demanded ₹50,000 from the complainant and subsequently reduced the amount to ₹35,000 before settling for ₹30,000. The bribe was demanded in return for showing official favour by not taking any further action against the complainant in connection with an allegation of electricity theft.

During the trap operation, the accused counted the bribe amount and kept the cash in the left-side back pocket of his trousers. The ACB officials subsequently recovered the tainted money from his pocket. He was arrested and would be produced before the Special Court for SPE and ACB Cases in Hyderabad for judicial remand. The case is under investigation.

articles.title: Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prices of prominent metals including gold, copper and aluminium tumbled to at least seven-month lows on hawkish commentary about U.S. Fed seeking to increase rates and weighing concerns over global economic growth in the immediate term.
Benchmark price of the yellow metal, that is, at the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) slipped to their lowest since September 2025 to close this week at $3,521.38 per troy ounce.
Further, benchmark price of copper – that is, at the London Metal Exchange (LME) – slipped to their lowest in about eight months at $12,230.40 per metric tonne.
Reference price for aluminium at LME also slipped to an almost one-year low at $2,824.5 per metric tonne.

Gold prices in 2026 have taken a nosedive from where they began the year, with the yellow metal falling over 25% from its peak, with a majority of the unwinding taking place over the last couple of months. Gold has seen exponential growth since 2022, rising 145% globally till now, with prices hitting multiple record highs last year.
Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Limited, says the primary driver of the downswing in gold prices is the change in global macroeconomic conditions.

“The biggest driver (in price movements) is that the macro story changed. Since the (Iran-U.S.) war, inflation expectations, energy prices, and anticipation of interest rate hikes capped gains for the metal.”

With traders expecting a more hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, the U.S. dollar has also gained strength in recent weeks. It is important to note that gold typically thrives in a weak-dollar environment.
U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s remarks last week further cemented expectations of a rate hike next month.
According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the target range to 4.00–4.25%.

Further, rising US Treasury yields have also added pressure on gold prices. Since gold is a non-interest-bearing asset, higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding the precious metal, making yield-bearing assets relatively more attractive.

Gold analysts expect the metal to trade range-bound over the next couple of quarters and into the beginning of FY28. The precious metal is expected to trade between $3,200 and $3,800 in the near term.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan entail for retirees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Story So Far: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in a meeting held in New Delhi on November 19, 2026 approved the Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings. As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal.

As of now, a retiring PF subscriber generally withdraws the entire provident fund accumulation as a lump sum. The proposal, cleared by the CBT, say an eligible member, upon retirement, may opt to receive their provident fund accumulations as monthly withdrawals; quarterly withdrawals; half-yearly withdrawals; or annual withdrawals. The remaining corpus will be invested within the EPF Fund and will continue to earn EPF interest on the running balance. The SWP scheme also proposes to provide flexible options to the member for enhancing his or her corpus in PF by voluntary contributions through payroll, direct additional contributions other than payroll and third-party micro-contributions.
